# Breadcrumbs

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use breadcrumbs to help users understand and move between levels in a website with a deep hierarchy.

## When to use

- Use when a site has multiple hierarchical levels and users need to understand or traverse that structure.
- Use the collapse-on-mobile variant for a long path after confirming that the first and final visible items remain useful.

## When not to use

- Do not use on a site with a flat information architecture.
- Do not use breadcrumbs to show progress through a linear transaction.
- Never show breadcrumbs together with a back link.

## Anatomy

- **Navigation landmark (required):** A nav element has a concise aria-label that identifies the breadcrumb navigation.
- **Ordered path (required):** An ordered list represents the hierarchy from the home page to the current page's parent.
- **Breadcrumb links (required):** Each item links to its corresponding ancestor level.

## Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default | `nav` | `govuk-breadcrumbs` | A short hierarchy on the standard page background. |
| Collapse on mobile | `nav` | `govuk-breadcrumbs`, `govuk-breadcrumbs--collapse-on-mobile` | A long path that should show only its first and last items on smaller screens. |
| Inverse | `nav` | `govuk-breadcrumbs`, `govuk-breadcrumbs--inverse` | A dark background with verified contrast. |

## Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- Place breadcrumbs before main so the page skip link bypasses them.
- Start at the site's home page and end at the parent of the current page; do not include the current page as a redundant final link.
- The component requires no JavaScript and every link must have a usable href.

## Accessibility contract

- Use a nav landmark with aria-label="Breadcrumb" or an equivalent localised label.
- Retain the ordered-list structure and meaningful link text.
- Verify inverse links and separators meet contrast requirements.

## Content rules

- Use the page or section name for each item and keep it concise.
- Ensure adjacent items are distinguishable when announced as a list of links.

## Token references

- `govuk.color.link`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.color.focus-text`
- `govuk.color.inverse-text`
- `govuk.breakpoint.tablet`

## HTML examples

### Three-level breadcrumbs

```html
<nav class="govuk-breadcrumbs" aria-label="Breadcrumb">
  <ol class="govuk-breadcrumbs__list">
    <li class="govuk-breadcrumbs__list-item"><a class="govuk-breadcrumbs__link" href="/">Home</a></li>
    <li class="govuk-breadcrumbs__list-item"><a class="govuk-breadcrumbs__link" href="/benefits">Benefits</a></li>
    <li class="govuk-breadcrumbs__list-item"><a class="govuk-breadcrumbs__link" href="/benefits/families">Families</a></li>
  </ol>
</nav>
```
